blocks.md: Here is Enbrel (Amgen) against Skyrizi, Rinvoq, Humira on the five rows the case asks for: approved uses, boxed warnings and safety fine print, dosing and convenience, patent and exclusivity timeline, and pricing and gross-to-net exposure. What limits Enbrel's growth is the Medicare negotiated price, worth about $342M a year in the base case, and the market has not clearly priced it in [1]. Tied finding: Enbrel is an IRA-selected drug whose Medicare negotiated price takes effect 2026-01-01, about $4,751 below the 30-day list price, which puts roughly $342M base ($2M bull to $681M bear) of annual revenue at risk [1]. Our call: the market has not clearly priced this in, on the analyst-attention, starter-thread and consensus tests [2].

blocks.md: Pipeline demonstration for the default ticker; not the team's Part 2 recommendation, which follows the company pick.

**No candidate clears the hurdle; least-bad option: Defend ENBREL through its US loss of exclusivity (EV -$5.2M)** [1]. ENBREL's company-stated US protection ends years before its immunology rivals' (cited 10-K patent tables); a contracting defense and a switch program value the retained revenue. No candidate has EV above zero, so none is chosen; Defend ENBREL through its US loss of exclusivity is the least-bad option on EV [1]. Budget: $80.0M committed over 24 months [1]; expected value -$5.2M, no payback within the horizon [1]. Decision needed: approve $80.0M over 24 months against $13,989.0M of cash and equivalents [2].

blocks.md: Pipeline demonstration for the default ticker; not the team's Part 2 recommendation, which follows the company pick.

blocks.text: Kill signals, first six to twelve months

blocks.md: The Defend ENBREL through its US loss of exclusivity move for Amgen rests on the findings below. Each signal names the filing or data row we will re-read, and the baseline it must move from; if two fire in the same quarter, leadership pauses the move and the valuation is re-run.

items: **Year-one net sales vs forecast**: < 80% of forecast by month 12 (company 10-Q product revenue; about 40 days after quarter end); action: replace the bear case with the observed path and re-run the valuation [1].

**Commercial coverage**: < 50% of commercial lives by month 6 (payer policy trackers (paid); proxy: company commentary; monthly to quarterly); action: update the scenario weights with the observed signal [2].

**Medicaid units vs plan**: < 80% of plan by month 9 (Medicaid SDUD (CMS); states submit within 60 days of quarter end; posting lags 1-2 quarters); action: replace the bear case with the observed path and re-run the valuation [3].

blocks.md: Check each signal at every 10-Q and after every earnings call. If the needle metric closes toward the peer median and the sealed forecast holds, the Defend ENBREL through its US loss of exclusivity commitment is released; if the Medicare or MFN signals fire instead, the move shifts toward Reprice. We publish the check, hit or miss, in the ledger.

Who decides its fate: Payers: CMS (Medicare negotiation) and Part D plan sponsors; Investors: analysts and holders who will read the next 10-Q and earnings call; Regulators: FDA (labels, exclusivity) and SEC (disclosure).

We pick the needle by a plain rule: the biggest cited impact that analysts asked about least. How rarely analysts asked: Already raised in part: the earnings-release headline scores 0.0 and analyst attention 0.2 (higher means more discussed); analysts' scorecard share for Medicare price negotiation is 0.2 [12]. Impact: Revenue lower from the Medicare negotiated price. Base case: Medicare spend of $3,904.5M with a 65.5% negotiated discount applied in full, less the 15% of rebates it no longer pays; bull and bear vary those shares (low-rebate class) [7][13][14].
Caveat: no finding at this company was rarely discussed; this is the best row from its least-discussed group.

blocks.md: Template stance, no valued move yet: options are ranked by rules on the verified findings; no budgeted move has been valued for this company.

**Move: Defend.** Fix the exposure the filings reveal (channel, receivables, margin, disclosure) before the market prices it. The verified findings behind it point the same way: customers are taking longer to pay than revenue growth explains, with operating income lower in the base case [1]. No budget is valued yet; the commitment is to act before the next quarterly filing.

memos.summary: Kill signals for the Defend move at AstraZeneca, with the cited baseline each must move from.

blocks.md: Template stance, no valued move yet: options are ranked by rules on the verified findings; no budgeted move has been valued for this company.

blocks.text: Kill signals, first six to twelve months

blocks.md: The Defend move for AstraZeneca rests on the findings below. Each signal names the filing or data row we will re-read, and the baseline it must move from; if two fire in the same quarter, leadership pauses the move and the valuation is re-run.

items: Receivables growth falls back inside revenue growth in the next two 10-Qs. Baseline today: DSO 64[derived: 1, 2, assumption] days vs 56[derived: 3, 4, assumption] a year earlier (+13.5%[derived: 1, 2, assumption, 3, 4]) (FY2025); peer median 72[assumption] days (0.7 sd below)[assumption][5][6][7][8][9][licensed source].

Inventory days fall back toward the peer median in the next two 10-Qs. Baseline today: Inventory 6,557[10][11] vs 5,288[10][12] a year earlier (+24.0%[derived: 11, 12], 2025 vs 2024) against annual revenue 58,739[derived: 2] vs 54,073[6][4] (+8.6%[derived: 2, 4]); gap +15.4 pts[derived: 11, 12, 2, 4]; peer median -4.5 pts[assumption] (1.3 sd above)[assumption] (peer figures computed, not page-cited)[7][8][9][licensed source].

CMS's next selected-drug list or MFP schedule leaves the product's exposure unchanged. Baseline today: Calquence's Medicare price is set by negotiation from January 2027: CMS Part B+D spend $1,614.2M[13]; base list discount 40%[14] (CMS-published analog, cited)[15][2][7][8][9][licensed source].
CMS's next selected-drug list or MFP schedule leaves the product's exposure unchanged.

blocks.md: Check each signal at every 10-Q and after every earnings call. If the needle metric closes toward the peer median and the sealed forecast holds, the Defend commitment is released; if the Medicare or MFN signals fire instead, the move shifts toward Reprice. We publish the check, hit or miss, in the ledger.

Who decides its fate: Payers: CMS (Medicare negotiation) and Part D plan sponsors; Investors: analysts and holders who will read the next 10-Q and earnings call; Regulators: FDA (labels, exclusivity) and SEC (disclosure).

What limits Keytruda's growth is loss of US exclusivity, worth about $5.35B a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [1][2]. Tied finding: Keytruda loses US exclusivity in 2028, and the first full year after entry has taken a median 28% of peak sales from comparable biologic products, about $5.35B base ($3.94B bull to $11.60B bear) on Keytruda's $18.83B of annual revenue [1][2]. Our call: the market has already priced this in, on the analyst-attention, starter-thread and consensus tests [3].

blocks.md: Here is Januvia (Merck) against Generic sitagliptin, Ozempic, Jardiance on the five rows the case asks for: approved uses, boxed warnings and safety fine print, dosing and convenience, patent and exclusivity timeline, and pricing and gross-to-net exposure. What limits Januvia's growth is loss of US exclusivity, worth about $880M a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [1]. Tied finding: Januvia loses US exclusivity in 2026, and the first full year after entry has taken a median 88% of peak sales from comparable small molecule products, about $880M base ($747M bull to $923M bear) on Januvia's $999M of annual revenue [1]. Our call: the market has already priced this in, on the analyst-attention, starter-thread and consensus tests [2].

blocks.md: Pipeline demonstration for the default ticker; not the team's Part 2 recommendation, which follows the company pick.

**Move: Move Keytruda patients to the subcutaneous formulation before the US loss of exclusivity.** Keytruda's label is the broadest in its class (cited label lines) and its company-stated US compound patent ends in 2028; moving patients to the subcutaneous formulation before then retains revenue the IV biosimilars would take. Selected on EV [1]. Budget: $794.3M committed over 24 months [1]; expected value $5,491.7M, payback month 18 [1]. Decision needed: approve $794.3M over 24 months against $6,849.0M of cash and equivalents [2].

items.value: Move Keytruda patients to the subcutaneous formulation before the US loss of exclusivity

blocks.md: The Move Keytruda patients to the subcutaneous formulation before the US loss of exclusivity move for Merck & Co. rests on the findings below. Each signal names the filing or data row we will re-read, and the baseline it must move from; if two fire in the same quarter, leadership pauses the move and the valuation is re-run.

items: **Year-one net sales vs forecast**: < 80% of forecast by month 12 (company 10-Q product revenue; about 40 days after quarter end); action: replace the bear case with the observed path and re-run the valuation [1].

blocks.md: Check each signal at every 10-Q and after every earnings call. If the needle metric closes toward the peer median and the sealed forecast holds, the Move Keytruda patients to the subcutaneous formulation before the US loss of exclusivity commitment is released; if the Medicare or MFN signals fire instead, the move shifts toward Reprice. We publish the check, hit or miss, in the ledger.

blocks.md: Template stance, no valued move yet: options are ranked by rules on the verified findings; no budgeted move has been valued for this company.

The verified findings behind it point the same way: medicare price setting reaches this product, with operating income lower in the base case [1]. No budget is valued yet; the commitment is to act before the next quarterly filing.

items: **Attack**: would press a label, dosing or safety advantage over rivals with prescribers and payers. Its findings carry smaller cited impacts than the needle; it is the fallback if the Reprice kill signals fire.

**Partner-or-buy**: would license or acquire to replace revenue at risk from earlier exclusivity loss, a narrower label or a dropped trial. Its findings (the label is narrower than rivals' [37][5]) carry smaller cited impacts than the needle; it is the fallback if the Reprice kill signals fire.

blocks.text: What would prove us wrong: kill signals, 6 to 12 months

items: CMS's next selected-drug list or MFP schedule leaves the product's exposure unchanged. Baseline: medicare price setting reaches this product [2][3].
Receivables growth falls back inside revenue growth in the next two 10-Qs. Baseline: customers are taking longer to pay than revenue growth explains [27][30].
The next 10-K drops or softens the new wording without a matching hit to results. Baseline: the filing wording changed [34].
Q3 2026 revenue growth lands outside our sealed forecast (80% interval -3.1% to +11.9%), which was hashed and committed before results [38].

Payers see a price they can score, investors see the five numbers and the kill signals they can re-check at the next 10-Q, and regulators see label and disclosure facts cited to the page.

excerpt.before: As regulators continue to focus on prescription drugs, our products are facing increased pressures across the portfolio. These pressures stem from legislative and policy changes, including price controls, pharmaceutical market access, discounting, changes to tax and importation laws and other restrictions in the U.S., EU and other regions around the world. These pressures have resulted in lower prices, lower reimbursement rates and smaller populations for whom payers will reimburse, which can negatively impact our results of operations (including intangible asset impairment charges), operating cash flow, liquidity and financial flexibility. In August 2024, as part of the first round of government price setting pursuant to the IRA, the HHS announced the "maximum fair price" for a 30-day equivalent supply of Eliquis , which applies to the U.S. Medicare channel effective January 1, 2026.

blocks.md: The Reprice move for Bristol Myers Squibb rests on the findings below. Each signal names the filing or data row we will re-read, and the baseline it must move from; if two fire in the same quarter, leadership pauses the move and the valuation is re-run.

items: CMS's next selected-drug list or MFP schedule leaves the product's exposure unchanged. Baseline today: Pomalyst's Medicare price is set by negotiation from January 2027: CMS Part B+D spend $2,069.1M[1]; base list discount 60%[2] (CMS-published analog, cited)[3][4][5][6][7][8][licensed source].

Receivables growth falls back inside revenue growth in the next two 10-Qs. Baseline today: Receivables 9,077[9][10] vs 9,711[11] a year earlier (-6.5%[derived: 10, 11], 2026Q2 vs 2025Q2) against quarterly revenue 12,973[12][13][6] vs 12,269[12][14][15] (+5.7%[derived: 6, 15]); gap -12.3 pts[derived: 10, 11, 6, 15]; peer median -0.3 pts[assumption] (1.7 sd below)[assumption] (peer figures computed, not page-cited).
The next 10-K drops or softens the new wording without a matching hit to results. Baseline today: New paragraph in MD&A vs FY2024 (topics: gtn, generic, pricing)[16].
Q3 2026 revenue growth lands outside our sealed forecast (80% interval -3.1% to +11.9%), which was hashed and committed before results [17].

blocks.md: Check each signal at every 10-Q and after every earnings call. If the needle metric closes toward the peer median and the sealed forecast holds, the Reprice commitment is released; if the Medicare or MFN signals fire instead, the move shifts toward Reprice. We publish the check, hit or miss, in the ledger.

Who decides its fate: Payers: CMS (Medicare negotiation) and Part D plan sponsors; Investors: analysts and holders who will read the next 10-Q and earnings call; Regulators: FDA (labels, exclusivity) and SEC (disclosure).

memos.summary: Wegovy vs Mounjaro, Zepbound, Foundayo on label, safety, dosing, exclusivity and pricing.

blocks.md: Here is Wegovy (Novo Nordisk) against Mounjaro, Zepbound, Foundayo on the five rows the case asks for: approved uses, boxed warnings and safety fine print, dosing and convenience, patent and exclusivity timeline, and pricing and gross-to-net exposure. What limits Wegovy's growth is the Medicare negotiated price, worth about $28M a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [1][2]. Tied finding: Wegovy is an IRA-selected drug whose Medicare negotiated price takes effect 2027-01-01, about $685 below the 30-day list price, which puts roughly $28M base ($3M bull to $52M bear) of annual revenue at risk [1][2]. Our call: the market has already priced this in, on the analyst-attention, starter-thread and consensus tests [3].

blocks.md: Here is Ozempic (Novo Nordisk) against Mounjaro, Zepbound, Foundayo on the five rows the case asks for: approved uses, boxed warnings and safety fine print, dosing and convenience, patent and exclusivity timeline, and pricing and gross-to-net exposure. What limits Ozempic's growth is the Medicare negotiated price, worth about $1.36B a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [1][2]. Tied finding: Ozempic is an IRA-selected drug whose Medicare negotiated price takes effect 2027-01-01, about $685 below the 30-day list price, which puts roughly $1.36B base ($143M bull to $2.57B bear) of annual revenue at risk [1][2]. Our call: the market has already priced this in, on the analyst-attention, starter-thread and consensus tests [3].

blocks.md: The Defend move for Novo Nordisk rests on the findings below. Each signal names the filing or data row we will re-read, and the baseline it must move from; if two fire in the same quarter, leadership pauses the move and the valuation is re-run.

items: Gross margin holds at the prior-year level in the next two quarterly reports. Baseline today: Gross margin 81.0%[derived: 1, 2] vs 84.7%[derived: 3, 4] a year earlier (-3.7 pts[derived: 1, 2, 3, 4]) (FY2025); peer median 74.1%[assumption] (1.1 sd above)[assumption][5][6][7][8][9][licensed source].

Inventory days fall back toward the peer median in the next two 10-Qs. Baseline today: Inventory 49,623[10][11] vs 40,849[10][12] a year earlier (+21.5%[derived: 11, 12], 2025 vs 2024) against annual revenue 309,064[derived: 2] vs 290,403[5][4] (+6.4%[derived: 2, 4]); gap +15.1 pts[derived: 11, 12, 2, 4]; peer median -4.5 pts[assumption] (1.3 sd above)[assumption] (peer figures computed, not page-cited)[7][8][9][licensed source].
No further impairment on the same asset in the next two filings. Baseline today: Impairment 2,760M[13] = 0.51%[derived: 14, 15] of assets (FY2025)[2][7][8][9][licensed source].
Gross margin holds at the prior-year level in the next two quarterly reports.

blocks.md: Check each signal at every 10-Q and after every earnings call. If the needle metric closes toward the peer median and the sealed forecast holds, the Defend commitment is released; if the Medicare or MFN signals fire instead, the move shifts toward Reprice. We publish the check, hit or miss, in the ledger.
Who decides its fate: Investors: analysts and holders who will read the next 10-Q and earnings call; Regulators: FDA (labels, exclusivity) and SEC (disclosure).

blocks.md: The Reprice move for AbbVie rests on the findings below. Each signal names the filing or data row we will re-read, and the baseline it must move from; if two fire in the same quarter, leadership pauses the move and the valuation is re-run.

items: CMS's next selected-drug list or MFP schedule leaves the product's exposure unchanged. Baseline today: Botox's Medicare price is set by negotiation from January 2028: CMS Part B+D spend $1,143.1M[1]; assumed base list discount 65.5%[derived: 2, 3] (median of the cycle 1-2 negotiated discounts in the CMS fact sheets; cited range 38%[4] to 85%[5]; no same-class MFP published)[6][7][8][9][10][11][licensed source].

The company's own disclosure puts the Medicaid MFN cost well below this estimate in the next 10-Q. Baseline today: ABBV signed an MFN agreement on 2026-01-12 that extends MFN pricing to Medicaid (R041); US investment pledge $100bn[derived: 12]; TrumpRx: Alphagan, Combigan, Humira, Synthroid (R042). Direction: adverse to US net price; size not disclosed (deal terms confidential), so no dollar figure is given[13][14][7][8][9][10][licensed source].

The effective tax rate reverts to the prior-year level in the next 10-Q. Baseline today: Effective tax rate 15.5%[derived: 15, 16] vs 39.4%[derived: 17, 18] a year earlier (-24.0 pts[derived: 15, 16, 17, 18]) (Q2 2026); peer median 17.7%[assumption] (0.4 sd below)[assumption][19][20].
Q3 2026 revenue growth lands outside our sealed forecast (80% interval +7.7% to +12.9%), which was hashed and committed before results [21].

blocks.md: Check each signal at every 10-Q and after every earnings call. If the needle metric closes toward the peer median and the sealed forecast holds, the Reprice commitment is released; if the Medicare or MFN signals fire instead, the move shifts toward Reprice. We publish the check, hit or miss, in the ledger.

Who decides its fate: Payers: CMS (Medicare negotiation) and Part D plan sponsors; Investors: analysts and holders who will read the next 10-Q and earnings call; Regulators: FDA (labels, exclusivity) and SEC (disclosure).

What limits Trulicity's growth is loss of US exclusivity, worth about $1.76B a year in the base case, and the market has not clearly priced it in [1][2]. Tied finding: Trulicity loses US exclusivity in 2027, and the first full year after entry has taken a median 28% of peak sales from comparable biologic products, about $1.76B base ($1.30B bull to $3.82B bear) on Trulicity's $6.20B of annual revenue [1][2]. Our call: the market has not clearly priced this in, on the analyst-attention, starter-thread and consensus tests [3].

blocks.md: **Move: Defend Trulicity through the 2027 loss of exclusivity and switch patients to Mounjaro.** Trulicity's Medicare price is set by negotiation from January 2028 and its US compound patent ends in 2027 (FY2025 10-K patent table); a rebate-wall defense and a Mounjaro switch program value the retained revenue. Strategic-fit rule excluded Seek new Zepbound indications to close the label gap with Wegovy (addresses no Part 1 finding); selected on EV among the rest [1]. Budget: $412.5M committed over 24 months [1]; expected value $597.8M, payback month 9 [1]. Decision needed: approve $412.5M over 24 months against $8,950.0M of cash and equivalents [2].

memos.summary: Kill signals for the Defend Trulicity through the 2027 loss of exclusivity and switch patients to Mounjaro move at Eli Lilly, with the cited baseline each must move from.

blocks.text: Kill signals, first six to twelve months

blocks.md: The Defend Trulicity through the 2027 loss of exclusivity and switch patients to Mounjaro move for Eli Lilly rests on the findings below. Each signal names the filing or data row we will re-read, and the baseline it must move from; if two fire in the same quarter, leadership pauses the move and the valuation is re-run.

items: **Year-one net sales vs forecast**: < 80% of forecast by month 12 (company 10-Q product revenue; about 40 days after quarter end); action: replace the bear case with the observed path and re-run the valuation [1].

**Commercial coverage**: < 50% of commercial lives by month 6 (payer policy trackers (paid); proxy: company commentary; monthly to quarterly); action: update the scenario weights with the observed signal [2].

**Medicaid units vs plan**: < 80% of plan by month 9 (Medicaid SDUD (CMS); states submit within 60 days of quarter end; posting lags 1-2 quarters); action: replace the bear case with the observed path and re-run the valuation [3].

blocks.md: Check each signal at every 10-Q and after every earnings call. If the needle metric closes toward the peer median and the sealed forecast holds, the Defend Trulicity through the 2027 loss of exclusivity and switch patients to Mounjaro commitment is released; if the Medicare or MFN signals fire instead, the move shifts toward Reprice. We publish the check, hit or miss, in the ledger.

Who decides its fate: Payers: CMS (Medicare negotiation) and Part D plan sponsors; Investors: analysts and holders who will read the next 10-Q and earnings call; Regulators: FDA (labels, exclusivity) and SEC (disclosure).

blocks.md: **Medicare price setting reaches this product.** Pfizer's Sharpest Needle is this: Ibrance's Medicare price is set by negotiation from January 2027: CMS Part B+D spend $1,984.6M[1]; base list discount 50%[2] (CMS-published analog, cited)[3][4][5][6][7][8][licensed source]. We pick the needle by a plain rule: the biggest cited impact that analysts asked about least. How rarely analysts asked: Already raised in part: the earnings-release headline scores 0.0 and analyst attention 0.5 (higher means more discussed); analysts' scorecard share for Medicare price negotiation is 0.5 [9]. Impact: Revenue lower from the Medicare negotiated price. Base case: Medicare spend of $1,984.6M with a 50% negotiated discount applied in full, less the 15% of rebates it no longer pays; bull and bear vary those shares (low-rebate class) [4][10][11].

What limits Ibrance's growth is loss of US exclusivity, worth about $3.63B a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [1]. Our call: the market has already priced this in, on the analyst-attention, starter-thread and consensus tests [2].

blocks.md: The Reprice move for Pfizer rests on the findings below. Each signal names the filing or data row we will re-read, and the baseline it must move from; if two fire in the same quarter, leadership pauses the move and the valuation is re-run.

items: CMS's next selected-drug list or MFP schedule leaves the product's exposure unchanged. Baseline today: Ibrance's Medicare price is set by negotiation from January 2027: CMS Part B+D spend $1,984.6M[1]; base list discount 50%[2] (CMS-published analog, cited)[3][4][5][6][7][8][licensed source].

The company's own disclosure puts the Medicaid MFN cost well below this estimate in the next 10-Q. Baseline today: PFE signed an MFN agreement on 2025-09-30 that extends MFN pricing to Medicaid (R002); US investment pledge $70bn[derived: 9]; TrumpRx: avg 50%[10], up to 85%[10] (R004). Direction: adverse to US net price; size not disclosed (deal terms confidential), so no dollar figure is given[11][12][4][5][6][7][licensed source].
The next 10-K drops or softens the new wording without a matching hit to results. Baseline today: New paragraph in MD&A vs FY2024 (topics: ira, mfn, gtn, 340b, pricing)[13].
Q3 2026 revenue growth lands outside our sealed forecast (80% interval -23.3% to +26.1%), which was hashed and committed before results [14].

blocks.md: Check each signal at every 10-Q and after every earnings call. If the needle metric closes toward the peer median and the sealed forecast holds, the Reprice commitment is released; if the Medicare or MFN signals fire instead, the move shifts toward Reprice. We publish the check, hit or miss, in the ledger.

Who decides its fate: Payers: CMS (Medicare negotiation) and Part D plan sponsors; Investors: analysts and holders who will read the next 10-Q and earnings call; Regulators: FDA (labels, exclusivity) and SEC (disclosure).

The IRA specifies a ceiling price but not a minimum price for selected drugs and does not require CMS to use a specific framework for determining selected drug prices. The selected products are subject to a government-established price for the Medicare population beginning in 2026. memos.summary: Every case product's growth limiter, tied finding and priced-in call on one page.

blocks.md: One line per case product: its growth limiter from the fine-print table, the financial finding it ties to, and our priced-in call. Products with a tied finding come first; which product is weakest is a judgment the table supports, not a score.

items: **Enbrel** (Amgen) vs Skyrizi, Rinvoq, Humira: growth limiter: What limits Enbrel's growth is the Medicare negotiated price, worth about $342M a year in the base case, and the market has not clearly priced it in [1]. Tied finding: Enbrel is an IRA-selected drug whose Medicare negotiated price takes effect 2026-01-01, about $4,751 below the 30-day list price, which puts roughly $342M base ($2M bull to $681M bear) of annual revenue at risk [1]. Priced in: not clearly.

**Farxiga** (AstraZeneca) vs Generic dapagliflozin, Jardiance: growth limiter: What limits Farxiga's growth is the Medicare negotiated price, worth about $381M a year in the base case, and the market has not clearly priced it in [2]. Tied finding: Farxiga is an IRA-selected drug whose Medicare negotiated price takes effect 2026-01-01, about $378 below the 30-day list price, which puts roughly $381M base ($12M bull to $750M bear) of annual revenue at risk [2]. Priced in: not clearly.

**Keytruda** (Merck & Co.) vs Opdivo, Imfinzi, Tecentriq: growth limiter: What limits Keytruda's growth is loss of US exclusivity, worth about $5.35B a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [3][4]. Tied finding: Keytruda loses US exclusivity in 2028, and the first full year after entry has taken a median 28% of peak sales from comparable biologic products, about $5.35B base ($3.94B bull to $11.60B bear) on Keytruda's $18.83B of annual revenue [3][4]. Priced in: yes.

**Januvia** (Merck & Co.) vs Generic sitagliptin, Ozempic, Jardiance: growth limiter: What limits Januvia's growth is loss of US exclusivity, worth about $880M a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [5]. Tied finding: Januvia loses US exclusivity in 2026, and the first full year after entry has taken a median 88% of peak sales from comparable small molecule products, about $880M base ($747M bull to $923M bear) on Januvia's $999M of annual revenue [5]. Priced in: yes.

**Eliquis** (Bristol Myers Squibb) vs Xarelto: growth limiter: What limits Eliquis's growth is loss of US exclusivity, worth about $12.72B a year in the base case, and the market has not clearly priced it in [6]. Tied finding: Eliquis loses US exclusivity in 2028, and the first full year after entry has taken a median 88% of peak sales from comparable small molecule products, about $12.72B base ($10.80B bull to $13.35B bear) on Eliquis's $14.44B of annual revenue [6]. Priced in: not clearly.

**Opdivo** (Bristol Myers Squibb) vs Keytruda, Tecentriq: growth limiter: What limits Opdivo's growth is loss of US exclusivity, worth about $68M a year in the base case, and the market has not clearly priced it in [7][8]. Tied finding: Opdivo loses US exclusivity in 2028, and the first full year after entry has taken a median 28% of peak sales from comparable biologic products, about $68M base ($50M bull to $147M bear) on Opdivo's $238M of annual revenue [7][8]. Priced in: not clearly.

**Wegovy** (Novo Nordisk) vs Mounjaro, Zepbound, Foundayo: growth limiter: What limits Wegovy's growth is the Medicare negotiated price, worth about $28M a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [9][10]. Tied finding: Wegovy is an IRA-selected drug whose Medicare negotiated price takes effect 2027-01-01, about $685 below the 30-day list price, which puts roughly $28M base ($3M bull to $52M bear) of annual revenue at risk [9][10]. Priced in: yes.

**Ozempic** (Novo Nordisk) vs Mounjaro, Zepbound, Foundayo: growth limiter: What limits Ozempic's growth is the Medicare negotiated price, worth about $1.36B a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [9][10]. Tied finding: Ozempic is an IRA-selected drug whose Medicare negotiated price takes effect 2027-01-01, about $685 below the 30-day list price, which puts roughly $1.36B base ($143M bull to $2.57B bear) of annual revenue at risk [9][10]. Priced in: yes.

**Zepbound** (Eli Lilly) vs Ozempic, Wegovy injection, Wegovy pill: growth limiter: What limits Zepbound's growth is the shift of volume to the lower cash price, worth about $3.14B a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [11]. Tied finding: The US cash price of $346 a month sits 68% below Zepbound's $1,086 list price, so every point of volume that moves to the cash channel gives up net revenue; on an assumed 10 to 40 percent of volume the range is $3.14B base ($1.26B bull to $5.02B bear) [11]. Priced in: yes.

**Trulicity** (Eli Lilly) vs Ozempic, Wegovy injection, Wegovy pill: growth limiter: What limits Trulicity's growth is loss of US exclusivity, worth about $1.76B a year in the base case, and the market has not clearly priced it in [12][13]. Tied finding: Trulicity loses US exclusivity in 2027, and the first full year after entry has taken a median 28% of peak sales from comparable biologic products, about $1.76B base ($1.30B bull to $3.82B bear) on Trulicity's $6.20B of annual revenue [12][13]. Priced in: not clearly.

**Ibrance** (Pfizer) vs Verzenio, Kisqali: growth limiter: What limits Ibrance's growth is loss of US exclusivity, worth about $3.63B a year in the base case, and the market has already priced it in [14]. Tied finding: Ibrance loses US exclusivity in 2027, and the first full year after entry has taken a median 88% of peak sales from comparable small molecule products, about $3.63B base ($3.08B bull to $3.81B bear) on Ibrance's $4.12B of annual revenue [14]. Priced in: yes.

**Repatha** (Amgen) vs Praluent, Leqvio, Lipfendra: growth limiter: The data do not support naming what limits Repatha's growth: no label-to-numbers channel had its inputs. No label row ties to a financial finding yet. Priced in: not clearly.

**Biktarvy** (Gilead Sciences) vs Dovato, Cabenuva: growth limiter: The data do not support naming what limits Biktarvy's growth: no label-to-numbers channel had its inputs. No label row ties to a financial finding yet. Priced in: not clearly.

**Yeztugo** (Gilead Sciences) vs Apretude: growth limiter: The data do not support naming what limits Yeztugo's growth: no label-to-numbers channel had its inputs. No label row ties to a financial finding yet. Priced in: not clearly.

**Tagrisso** (AstraZeneca) vs Rybrevant (with Lazcluze), Lazcluze (with Rybrevant): growth limiter: The data do not support naming what limits Tagrisso's growth: no label-to-numbers channel had its inputs. No label row ties to a financial finding yet. Priced in: not clearly.

**Imfinzi** (AstraZeneca) vs Keytruda: growth limiter: The data do not support naming what limits Imfinzi's growth: no label-to-numbers channel had its inputs. No label row ties to a financial finding yet. Priced in: not clearly.

**Skyrizi** (AbbVie) vs Tremfya, Stelara, Cosentyx, Entyvio, Amjevita (Humira biosimilar): growth limiter: The data do not support naming what limits Skyrizi's growth: no label-to-numbers channel had its inputs. No label row ties to a financial finding yet. Priced in: not clearly.

**Rinvoq** (AbbVie) vs Tremfya, Cosentyx, Entyvio, Amjevita (Humira biosimilar): growth limiter: The data do not support naming what limits Rinvoq's growth: no label-to-numbers channel had its inputs. No label row ties to a financial finding yet. Priced in: not clearly.

**Mounjaro** (Eli Lilly) vs Ozempic, Wegovy injection, Wegovy pill: growth limiter: The data do not support naming what limits Mounjaro's growth: no label-to-numbers channel had its inputs. No label row ties to a financial finding yet. Priced in: not clearly.

**Vyndamax (Vyndaqel family)** (Pfizer) vs Attruby, Amvuttra: growth limiter: The data do not support naming what limits Vyndamax (Vyndaqel family)'s growth: no label-to-numbers channel had its inputs. No label row ties to a financial finding yet. Priced in: not clearly.

**Tremfya** (Johnson & Johnson) vs Skyrizi, Rinvoq, Wezlana (Stelara biosimilar): growth limiter: The data do not support naming what limits Tremfya's growth: no label-to-numbers channel had its inputs. No label row ties to a financial finding yet. Priced in: not clearly.

**Darzalex** (Johnson & Johnson) vs Sarclisa: growth limiter: The data do not support naming what limits Darzalex's growth: no label-to-numbers channel had its inputs. No label row ties to a financial finding yet. Priced in: not clearly.

blocks.md: 3 of the 10 companies carry a DECIDE output [4]: one CEO move valued against two alternatives on the same five numbers (expected value, cash at risk, payback month, scenario spread, MCDA) with kill signals. Demo flags are stated per line. The other 7 (Gilead Sciences, AstraZeneca, Bristol Myers Squibb, Novo Nordisk, AbbVie, Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson) carry template stances with no valued move yet [4].

items: **Amgen** (pipeline demonstration, not the team's recommendation): no candidate clears the hurdle; least-bad option: Defend ENBREL through its US loss of exclusivity, expected value -$5.2M on $80.0M committed over 24 months, no payback within the horizon [1]. No candidate has EV above zero, so none is chosen; Defend ENBREL through its US loss of exclusivity is the least-bad option on EV [1].

**Merck & Co.** (pipeline demonstration, not the team's recommendation): chosen move: Move Keytruda patients to the subcutaneous formulation before the US loss of exclusivity, expected value $5,491.7M on $794.3M committed over 24 months, payback month 18 [2]. Selected on EV [2].

**Eli Lilly** (valued move): chosen move: Defend Trulicity through the 2027 loss of exclusivity and switch patients to Mounjaro, expected value $597.8M on $412.5M committed over 24 months, payback month 9 [3]. Strategic-fit rule excluded Seek new Zepbound indications to close the label gap with Wegovy (addresses no Part 1 finding); selected on EV among the rest [3].

memos.prompt: Where was the AI confidently wrong?
aliases: where the ai was confidently wrong
what did the ai get wrong
how did you catch ai errors
memos.summary: 26 logged cases where the AI was confidently wrong, with how each was caught and fixed.

blocks.md: Yes, 26 times that we logged [1]. Each case records what the model claimed, who or what caught it and the fix; none was caught by asking the model again. Here are 8 of the 26 [1], from the first backtest to the data layer.

rows: v1 backtest: gross-margin drops precede an adverse event 59% of the time vs a 43% base rate [2]
two skeptics, then each read the other [2]
Point-in-time windows; firm-clustered interval must clear 1. Only margin compression survives (12% with no flags to 61% with five); no flag predicts revenue drops or impairments [2]
First citation gate: "verified" on 4 shown z-scores and 4 product counts [3]
independent re-check of the gate output (verify2) [3]
The gate accepted any numeral on the cited page (an EPS of 1.18, an I/B/E/S row of -0.13, a page footer "- 3 -"). Verified now means in the quoted span or the citation's own value ... [3]
AMGN needle from the code: receivables up faster than revenue, a collections flag [4]
Receivables track gross invoices to three wholesalers (75% of receivables); gross billing grew 15.4% vs net revenue 9.7%, with a separate rebate liability ... [4]
Quotes from fool.com transcripts, which open with LLM-written takeaways that read like call text [5]
Corpus flags the summaries and a mislabeled AZN Q1 transcript; the verifier rejects quotes from those sections. ABBV and AMGN each had one such line avoided [5]
MRK needle: R&D at 58.7% of revenue [6]
One-time $5.7B acquired IPR&D charge ($2.31 per share) that also drove a -95.8% tax rate. One-offs go to context, not signals [6]
AMGN: $7.6B IRS claim vs $4.4B reserve is a $3.2B unreserved gap [7]
Accrued interest and penalties add $1.9B (reserve about $6.3B); the gap is at least $1.3B and a base case with two assumptions [7]
Page numbers on quotes (AMGN 10-Q Enbrel, TEPEZZA and BLINCYTO sentences; BMY revenue tables) [8]
The quote was on the neighbouring file page; 20+ citations rejected and re-cited to the right file page and printed page [8]
Data layer: 616 rows of "restated" product revenue [9]
Zero true restatements; 447 were recasts where a company moved products between lines [9]

blocks.md: Every case cites its evidence file or commit; the full log is docs/ai_in_the_build.md. Only verified rows are citable anywhere in this app.

memos.prompt: What are the honest limits of this analysis?
aliases: what are the honest limits of this analysis
memos.summary: 26 stated limits: data we lack and the proxy we use, and limits of the method.

blocks.md: These are the limits we state in the pitch, grouped into data we do not have (with the proxy we use instead) and limits of the method itself. Every sentence is the one in docs/honest_limits.md.

blocks.text: Data we do not have, and the proxy we use

rows: No product-level net price is public, so we never claim one. [1]
Company-level gross-to-net disclosures, Medicare Part B ASP (net-like), Part D gross spend, NADAC (list-like) and Medicaid SDUD; a 50 / 60 / 70% GTN band labelled as inference [1]
Filings give ex-US revenue but not units or price, so our policy and patent math covers the US only. [2]
US revenue from the filing's geographic split [2]
PBM formulary and rebate contracts are private. [3]
Medicare Part D claims, company commentary and published coverage-lag studies (6 to 12 months) [3]
Most Q3 results land after judging; our numbers run through Q2 2026. [4]
Up to nine directional calls sealed by hash before the results (J&J reported before our cut-off) [4]
MFN rate has no public source
The MFN rate has no public source: deal terms are confidential. We score MFN as a direction, not a dollar amount, except where a company states its own effect. [5]
The agreement, its date and the company's US revenue share; Pfizer's Medicaid base rate is used only to rank, never printed ... [5]
No HIV drug has a published negotiated Medicare price (the Biktarvy price takes effect in 2028), so Gilead's Biktarvy exposure is a range, not a point. [6]
The full range of published cuts (38%, 65.5% median, 85%) at the low-rebate rule; under the alternative formula Gilead's score moves about 10% and its rank does not change [6]
We have no short-interest data, so we cannot see whether short sellers already positioned on a finding. [7]
The term is set to "no information" and flagged on every row, which makes obscurity optimistic for heavily shorted names [7]
Analyst consensus data are licensed; the numbers feed our math but are shown only in the local app. [8]
The noise scale (σ) and consensus test run locally; public output shows the result, not the rows [8]
Receivables signals need a footnote read
A receivables or inventory ratio is a flag for a human read, never a finding by itself. [9]
Two of our own code flags were explained by the footnotes (AMGN by gross billing to three wholesalers with a separate rebate liability, AZN by factored receivables and bank acceptance drafts) ... [9]
Label exclusivity is not from labels
Labels carry no patent dates; our exclusivity dates come from each 10-K's patent table and the Orange and Purple Books. [10]
The company-stated date on the cited 10-K page; later-listed use and formulation patents and Purple Book reference exclusivity are shown as secondary ... [10]
Text fragments checked against our page text
Our quote links highlight the text in the source, but we checked each fragment against our stored copy of the page, not against live EDGAR. [11]
The stored page text the verifier uses; Chrome and Edge highlight on open; table rows split across cells link to the page without a highlight [11]
I/B/E/S and XBRL citations have no page link
Analyst consensus and XBRL-derived figures are cited by data row or concept, not by a page you can open. [12]
Each footnote names the I/B/E/S row or XBRL concept and its operands; derived numbers recompute from cited operands [12]
Label-breadth channel sized on Medicare coverage
We size a label difference by what Medicare Part D covers, because commercial coverage is private. [13]
Part D claims and gross spend for the products compared; commercial uptake is not estimated [13]
The page-highlight viewer runs on our machine; the public footnotes give the file page, the printed page and a link to the document. [14]
SEC text fragments, PDF `#page=` links, DailyMed label pages [14]
The model-written prose and courtroom trial run once, cached, when the API key is armed; every number you see today is deterministic code. [15]
Deterministic sentences from the same cited records; the gate is identical for both tracks [15]
Backtest raw panel not on disk
Our signal track record comes from one 43-firm backtest whose summary we keep but whose raw panel we cannot re-run tonight. [16]
The committed hit rates, haircut 26% for data mining, shown as tiers (within about a factor of two); peer-level outliers get no track-record credit until tested [16]
Analyst attention is measured from up to ten earnings calls, and outside nine scored topics it comes from a keyword match. [17]
The priced-in scorecard for nine topics; a regex over analyst turns for the rest; the scorecard median, flagged, when nothing matches [17]
Every footnote opens the source document, but the page-highlight viewer runs only in our local app. [18]
SEC text-fragment links (Chrome and Edge highlight the quote), PDF page links, plain DailyMed label pages, and the file page and printed page in every footnote [18]

items: **Track records are tiers**: Signal track records come from one 43-firm, between-firm backtest and published return studies; they rank evidence types to within about a factor of two and are shown as tiers, not exact probabilities. [19]
**Text and call findings**: Text and call findings without a mapped dollar channel are shown with their evidence tier and no dollar figure, and stay out of the top-five table. [20]
**Noise scale**: Materiality divides by the company's usual quarterly EPS miss, annualized by an assumed factor of two; impacts one to two years out are compared on that near-term scale. [21]
**Consensus test**: When consensus for the affected year did not exist before the disclosure, we cannot test whether analysts priced it, and we assume a 50% chance they did. [22]

**Foreign filers**: AstraZeneca and Novo Nordisk have no earnings release in our index, so their headline term is imputed from the other eight; Novo's dollar-based policy channels are not converted. [23]
**Coverage**: Several signal families in the design (insider sales, 8-K items, misstatement scores, gross-to-net, footnotes) have no detector yet; patent-loss inputs are thin for four companies. [24]

**DECIDE**: Scenario weights are a launch base rate applied to every move, and the bear and bull multipliers are boundary values, so the scenario spread is understated and the value leans optimistic. [25]
**Facts**: 69,553 facts in the store, 10,963 of them page-verified. [26]

memos.prompt: How does NEEDLE work?
memos.summary: Four outputs: findings table, Sharpest Needle, product fine print, DECIDE; verified to the page, gated per number, sealed forecasts.

blocks.md: **Four outputs.** First, a findings table: every verified finding with its source page, impact math, peer comparison and confidence, ranked by dollar impact. Second, the Sharpest Needle, by a plain rule: the biggest cited impact that analysts asked about least. Third, the product fine-print table: approved uses, safety, dosing, exclusivity and pricing for each case product against its rivals, with a growth limiter and a priced-in call. Fourth, DECIDE: one CEO move with a budget, compared with two alternatives on the same five numbers (expected value, cash at risk, payback month, scenario spread, MCDA), with kill signals for the first 6 to 12 months. **Verify to the page.** A finding survives only if its quote is on the cited page and every figure is found there or derived from figures that are; the rest go to a rejected log (279 rows so far [3]) [1]. **Numeric gate.** Every number printed here carries a marker to its page, its derivation or its stated assumption; rows that fail the gate are excluded, oversized impacts withheld, licensed data never printed [1]. **Sealed forecasts.** Revenue forecasts for 7 companies were hashed (sha256) and committed before Q3 results [4]. Calibrated on 1793 firm-quarters, the forecaster's interval covered 0.794 against a 0.8 target [5]; a blind test on J&J's Q3 release landed inside it [6]. **Ledger.** Every run appends to a hash-chained ledger (110 records, intact at export [7]). **Honesty.** The CEO memo is drafted by rules from verified findings and the DECIDE numbers, not by a model, and says so; the cases where the AI was confidently wrong are logged with their fixes [2].
